# File-type filtering in ripgrep

ripgrep's `-t`/`-T`/`--type-add` behavior lives almost entirely in one file:
`crates/ignore/src/types.rs`. It defines what a "file type" is, how a set of
selections compiles into a matcher, and how that matcher answers "does this
path count as this type" for every file the directory walker visits. The
default catalog of extensions lives separately, in
`crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs`.

## Representing a definition

A type is a `FileTypeDef { name: String, globs: Vec<String> }` — a name plus
every glob that recognizes it. `TypesBuilder` accumulates these in a
`HashMap<String, FileTypeDef>` keyed by name, alongside a separate
`Vec<Selection<()>>` recording what the caller actually asked for. `Selection<T>`
is a small enum, `Select(String, T)` or `Negate(String, T)`, generic so it can
hold either `()` while the builder is accumulating names or a resolved
`FileTypeDef` once `build()` has looked the name up.

`TypesBuilder::add` inserts one glob under a name, rejecting `"all"` (reserved,
see below) and any name containing a non-alphanumeric character.
`add_def` parses the string forms accepted by `--type-add`: `"name:glob"` adds
one glob directly, and `"name:include:a,b,c"` copies every glob currently
registered under `a`, `b`, and `c` into `name` — a snapshot at the time it's
called, not a live alias, so a later `--type-add` to `a` won't retroactively
extend `name`. `add_defaults` walks the `DEFAULT_TYPES` table in
`default_types.rs`, a `&[(&[&str], &[&str])]` of alias lists to glob lists,
kept lexicographically sorted (a test at the bottom of that file asserts the
first alias of each entry sorts correctly).

## Building the matcher

`TypesBuilder::build` turns the accumulated names and selections into a
`Types`. For each `Selection` it resolves the name against `self.types`
(`Error::UnrecognizedFileType` if missing), clones the `FileTypeDef`, and feeds
every one of its globs into a single `GlobSetBuilder`, compiled with
`.literal_separator(true)`. Two bookkeeping structures fall out of that loop:
`glob_to_selection: Vec<(usize, usize)>` maps each glob's position in the
built `GlobSet` back to `(selection index, glob index within that
definition's list)`, and `has_selected` records whether at least one
`Selection::Select` (as opposed to only negations) was ever pushed. The
resulting `Types` also keeps a sorted `Vec<FileTypeDef>` (via
`definitions()`, used by `--type-list`) and an `Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>` — a
reusable scratch buffer for match indices, since `matched()` runs once per
file across a directory tree that may be walked from many threads.

## Matching a path

`Types::matched` bypasses directories and empty glob sets immediately,
returning `Match::None`. Otherwise it extracts only the file name (via
`pathutil::file_name`) — type globs never see the rest of the path — and asks
the `GlobSet` for every matching glob index via `matches_into`, which fills a
vector in ascending index order. The highest index, i.e. the *last* one,
wins: `Types::matched` takes `matches.last()`, looks it up in
`glob_to_selection` to find the owning `Selection`, and returns
`Match::Whitelist` or `Match::Ignore` depending on whether that selection was
a `Select` or a `Negate`. Because glob indices are assigned in the order
selections were built, this means **the selection added last takes
precedence whenever two selections' globs both match the same path** — the
crate's own tests exercise exactly this (`matchnot3`/`matchnot4` in the
`#[cfg(test)]` block negate a type added after a conflicting select, and vice
versa, to pin the tie-break both ways). If nothing matches but `has_selected`
is true, the path is still `Match::Ignore` — once any `-t` is given, ripgrep
switches to whitelist-only mode for files.

## Where it sits in the walker

`crates/ignore/src/dir.rs` calls `self.0.types.matched(path, is_dir)` only
after checking overrides (`-g`/`--glob`) and ignore-file rules, and only if
neither of those already decided the match — so type filtering has the lowest
precedence of the three, and, since `matched` bails out on `is_dir`, it never
prunes directory traversal, only files. `IgnoreInner` stores the matcher as
`Arc<Types>`, so descending into a subdirectory clones an `Arc`, not the
`GlobSet`.

## Wiring from the CLI

`crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs::types` builds the real `Types` per invocation:
`TypesBuilder::new()`, `add_defaults()`, then a `TypeChange::{Clear, Add,
Select, Negate}` for each of `--type-clear`, `--type-add`, `-t`/`--type`, and
`-T`/`--type-not`, replayed **in the order the flags were parsed**
(`crates/core/flags/lowargs.rs` holds them as `Vec<TypeChange>`). That ordering
is exactly what feeds the last-selection-wins rule above, so `-t rust
--type-not rust` and `--type-not rust -t rust` are not equivalent. The name
`"all"` is handled inside `select`/`negate` themselves by iterating
`self.types.keys()` at call time, so its effect also depends on whether it's
placed before or after any `--type-add` that introduces new names.

## Contributor notes

Type names are restricted to Unicode letters and digits; `"all"` and anything
with punctuation is rejected by `TypesBuilder::add`. New default types belong
in `default_types.rs` and must stay sorted. Tests for matching semantics live
in the `matched!` macro at the bottom of `types.rs` — new precedence or
`include` behavior should get a case there, not just an integration test.
